title: Terms & Compliance: Bid Evaluation + Pricing Committee Intake
summary: Initial procurement intake for vendor gating: MSA/DPA expectations, KMS/SSO requirements, pricing thresholds for pricing committee, and pilot scope. AE + SE introduced Redwood deployment modes and outlined security artifacts. Legal has open questions on liability caps and data residency. Next: send security pack, pricing bands, and schedule technical pilot runbook meeting.
action_items: Maya Patel: Send security packet (SOC2 + encryption whitepaper) and initial pricing bands - due 2026-03-03
Ethan Chen: Share sample pilot runbook and recommend instance types for Civitas workload - due 2026-03-05
Emily Ortiz (Civitas): Highlight DPA clauses that need redlines and circulate to procurement - due 2026-03-06
Samir Rao (Civitas): Provide current KMS provider details and SSO metadata - due 2026-03-04
Lara Kline (Civitas): Schedule pricing committee review for week of 2026-03-08 - due 2026-03-02
next_steps: Redwood to email security packet + pricing bands
Customer legal to return DPA redlines
SE-led pilot technical runbook review scheduled after redlines
Pricing committee meeting to decide commit threshold
header: Date: 2026-03-01 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 47 min | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Ethan Chen (Redwood SE); Lara Kline (Civitas Procurement); Samir Rao (Civitas Security); Emily Ortiz (Civitas Legal); Noah Velasquez (CTO)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call? Maya here from Redwood. Ethan's with me - he'll cover the tech bits.
[00:08] Lara Kline: Lara here. uh procurement side. Samir here as well.
[00:12] Samir Rao: Samir - security. Emily - legal is on. Noah will jump in - he might be late.
[00:18] Ethan Chen: Cool, thanks. agenda I proposed was quick intro to Redwood offering, call out deployment modes, security artifacts, then pricing thresholds for your pricing committee, then any DPA/MSA redlines. Is that good?
[00:28] Lara Kline: Yep that works. high level we need to decide whether we can go hosted or require private VPC with KMS. pricing committee is tight if commit is above our X threshold.
[00:36] Noah Velasquez: (joined) Sorry running late. I can jump in on infra Qs.
[00:40] Maya Patel: No worries Noah. quick primer: Redwood provides hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC / on-prem). Most customers start hosted for speed to value, then move to dedicated for commit guarantees, or private for regulated data.
[00:55] Emily Ortiz: quick process note: we'll need the MSA and DPA to go to our legal review. typical asks: liability cap, data residency commitments, and subprocessor list. can you share a redlineable DPA?
[01:05] Maya Patel: Yep. we'll send our standard MSA + DPA and a security packet. note there are some differences between hosted and private re: egress fees and keying.
[01:12] Samir Rao: on keying—do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM? we need to know if keys can be in our cloud KMS or if Redwood retains any key material.
[01:19] Ethan Chen: short answer—yes, for Private we support customer-managed KMS and BYOK. for Dedicated we have options: either Redwood-managed keys or integrations with your cloud KMS via envelope encryption. some customers do HSM with our private package.
[01:31] Samir Rao: envelope.. hm okay. will want detail. also curious about token logs and audit retention. we prefer not to log raw payloads.
[01:38] Maya Patel: understood. our security packet includes token-level retention policies, pseudonymization options, and SIEM hooks. some of that depends on deployment mode. in hosted we have longer retention by default but can set contractual limits.
[01:48] Lara Kline: pricing committee question — what's the typical switch-over commit where customers go from hosted to dedicated? we need bands.
[01:55] Ethan Chen: most mid-market customers move when sustained monthly token usage crosses the equivalent of a few hundred GPU-hours — but pricing bands vary by model. we'll share a pricing band spreadsheet after this call.
[02:06] Lara Kline: for procurement we need a ballpark today for routing to the committee. can you give a green / yellow / red cost estimate?
[02:12] Maya Patel: green = under $15k/mo (stay hosted, standard SLAs), yellow = $15-70k/mo (consider dedicated with some reserved capacity), red = >$70k/mo (definitely look at dedicated contract or private deployment). these are rough and we'll send specifics.
[02:27] Noah Velasquez: what's the SLA for latency? our product requires p95 latency under 300ms for small prompt sizes otherwise user experience suffers.
[02:35] Ethan Chen: latency SLAs differ by deployment. hosted SLAs focus on availability and throughput, whereas Dedicated has tighter p95 latency targets depending on instance tier. for your 300ms p95 we’d recommend a Dedicated pool sized for your QPS, with warm KV cache strategies.
[02:52] Samir Rao: small correction — we need data residency in EU for certain datasets, can Redwood guarantee region pinning?
[02:58] Maya Patel: yes region pinning possible for Dedicated and Private. Hosted API can be regionally restricted but has multi-region fallbacks; we can contractually pin model serving to eu-west-1 for your tenant.
[03:10] Emily Ortiz: on DPA—what about subprocessors? we need a current list and notification timeline for new subs.
[03:15] Maya Patel: we publish a subprocessor list in the security packet and provide 30 days notice for new ones.
[03:20] Lara Kline: any data escrow or code escrow options?
[03:23] Maya Patel: for enterprise private deployments we can discuss escrow. it's not standard for hosted customers.
[03:28] Samir Rao: another security question — are raw customer requests stored for troubleshooting? some vendors store request payloads for 30 days.
[03:33] Ethan Chen: by default we keep traces for 7-14 days for debugging; can be contractually limited and payloads can be redacted or not persisted depending on requirements. again depends on deployment.
[03:43] Lara Kline: procurement needs to know termination assistance and data deletion timeline for the MSA.
[03:48] Maya Patel: our standard is 90 days for retention after contract termination with options to accelerate deletion to 30 days on negotiation. we include certified deletion proof on request.
[03:56] Emily Ortiz: liability caps — we usually cap at X times fees or a fixed amount. what's Redwood's standard?
[04:00] Maya Patel: standard is fees in prior 12 months, with carveouts for gross negligence. we can discuss upper caps in enterprise SOWs.
[04:09] Emily Ortiz: we'll likely propose an alternative cap; can you flag which clauses are negotiable?
[04:13] Maya Patel: yes we'll annotate the MSA. legal folks typically negotiate liability, indemnities, and data residency clauses.
[04:18] Lara Kline: procurement process timeline — we run pricing committee Thursday, vendor intake Friday. we need information by Wednesday EOD to make the packet.
[04:25] Maya Patel: noted — we'll prioritize sending the security packet and a pricing band doc by Wednesday EOD.
[04:29] Noah Velasquez: about pilot — we want to run a 2-week pilot generating embeddings + reranking on proprietary dataset. what's the onboarding friction?
[04:38] Ethan Chen: doable. typical pilot steps: auth set up (API keys or SSO), sample dataset ingest, run baseline eval, benchmarking for latency and cost, then iterate. I'll send a pilot runbook with recommended instance sizes and a checklist.
[04:52] Samir Rao: concerning SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and Okta; can you integrate SSO for RBAC?
[04:57] Ethan Chen: yes, we support SAML/SSO and can wire up Okta for user provisioning and role-based access controls. Private deployments get deeper RBAC hooks.
[05:05] Lara Kline: billing model — do you do committed usage discounts or overage billing?
[05:10] Maya Patel: both. committed reserved capacity for Dedicated gets discount tiers; hosted is pay-as-you-go with volume pricing. we also offer hybrid: reserved baseline + burst on hosted.
[05:22] Emily Ortiz: one more legal detail — do you offer audit rights? our security policy sometimes requires on-site audits or third-party SOC reports.
[05:29] Maya Patel: we provide SOC 2 Type II and can accommodate third-party pen test reports. on-site audits are rare but possible under enterprise terms.
[05:36] Lara Kline: ok this is helpful. procurement will want a one-pager for the pricing committee: commitment options, estimated bands, and required approvals.
[05:44] Maya Patel: we'll prepare a one-pager and the pricing band spreadsheet.
[05:47] Ethan Chen: quick technical note — you mentioned KV cash "cache" earlier; for reranking workloads we'll recommend proactive prefix caching and batch size tuning to meet your 300ms p95. also watch out for prompt length blow-outs which drive GPU time.
[06:02] Noah Velasquez: for embeddings we have longer sequences sometimes; any quantization or model recommendations?
[06:08] Ethan Chen: for embeddings, smaller dedicated models or quantized variants usually do fine. Redwood Optimize (we sometimes call it Redwood Optima in internal notes) gives quantization suggestions per workload. we'll include model recommendations in the runbook.
[06:21] Samir Rao: curious about retention and legal hold — if a law enforcement hold comes in, what's your process?
[06:27] Maya Patel: we escalate to compliance, preserve requested data, and work with your legal counsel. we provide logs and a timestamped chain of custody as part of enterprise compliance workflows.
[06:35] Emily Ortiz: in the DPA we may request a clause about notification timing for breaches. what's Redwood's standard notice window?
[06:40] Maya Patel: standard is 72 hours for confirmed incidents, subject to law. we'll put that in the packet but are open to discussion in enterprise terms.
[06:49] Lara Kline: (interrupt) procurement will also ask about subcontractor location — any subs outside EU/US?
[06:53] Maya Patel: yes some infra subs may be in other regions; the subprocessor list will have details. for EU-only constraints, Private deployment is the path.
[07:02] Noah Velasquez: for the pilot we'd like to test with our internal telemetry turned on. will that add to cost?
[07:08] Ethan Chen: telemetry adds minimal cost; main cost driver is tokens and GPU time. we'll model that in the pilot estimate.
[07:15] Samir Rao: one more — encryption in transit: TLS versions? we require TLS1.2 minimum and prefer 1.3.
[07:20] Ethan Chen: we support TLS1.2 and 1.3; we'll include cipher suite details in the security pack.
[07:27] Lara Kline: any other blockers from legal side at this point? Emily?
[07:31] Emily Ortiz: just liability caps and maybe data residency clauses. once we get the DPA we'll flag redlines.
[07:36] Maya Patel: perfect. to recap we'll send: MSA/DPA, security packet (SOC2, subprocessor list, KMS options), pricing bands, and a pilot runbook.
[07:45] Lara Kline: timeline again - need paperwork by Wednesday EOD for Thursday pricing review.
[07:50] Maya Patel: understood - Wednesday EOD.
[07:53] Noah Velasquez: ok let's do the pilot after the DPA is acceptable. we'll schedule SE runbook call next week.
[07:58] Ethan Chen: I'll propose slots for the runbook review.
[08:02] Maya Patel: great — thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the packet and links.
[08:06] Lara Kline: thanks all.
[08:08] Emily Ortiz: thanks.
[08:10] (meeting ends)
